perspective:
Harold Padilla’s available information:

- He knows himself as Harold Padilla, a project manager, and sees himself as empathetic/people-oriented. He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer and trusted friend whose advice he often seeks.
- In the coffee-shop meeting, Harold felt frustrated and anxious because he believed his project team was unmotivated and progress was suffering. He told Arthur this. He heard Arthur advise understanding each team member’s individual motivation and having one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood. Harold decided to try this and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold felt hopeful and relieved. He told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand their motivations. He heard Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each of them and asked them to make the project a success together.
- Later, Harold observed that the team still was not responding well despite using Arthur’s advice. He felt disappointed and worried about the project. He told Arthur this. Arthur suggested there might be deeper issues—personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors—and that Harold might need to dig deeper. Harold decided to set up another round of meetings and thanked Arthur.
- Harold then felt determined and focused, believing there might be underlying team issues he had not addressed. He held one-on-one meetings and asked team members to share concerns. Team Member 1 told him there was tension among a few people affecting work. Team Member 2 told him they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts and try to redistribute tasks, and told them their well-being was important.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve team performance. He told the team he would implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive and open environment. He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and helpful, and Team Member 2 agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed. Harold said he was glad and emphasized teamwork, input, and well-being.
